Here's the thing: I have a laptop with the exact same video card, and I ran into very similar problems, very nearly pulling out all my hair trying to get any *buntu flavor to install -- and let's not even talk about BSD. The thing that saved me was a kernel parameter you can set at boot time to tell the system to stop trying to load video drivers: nomodeset. The reader's digest version is that you interrupt the installer's grub so that you can pass kernel parameters, give it the "nomodeset" option on the boot line, and go through the entire install process that way. On reboot, you may have to insert it into the boot string of the actual system, at least until you can get the NVidia drivers loaded, but you won't need it after that.
